newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS TAKE "WINTER CHAMPIONSHIP" WITHOUT KICKING BALL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS TAKE "WINTER CHAMPIONSHIP" WITHOUT KICKING BALL.

text.p: League leaders Juventus won Serie A's "Winter Championship" on Sunday without even kicking a ball.

Second-placed Sampdoria's last-gasp draw at Fiorentina and third-placed Inter's first defeat at home to Bologna in 20 years secured Juventus the accolade traditionally awarded to the team leading Serie A at its halfway stage.

The Turin side have 30 points from 17 matches and are one point ahead of Sampdoria and two in front of Inter -- although the gap will widen if Juve beat Lazio in a late-night match at Rome's Olympic stadium later on Sunday.
In the 64 Serie A tournaments to date, the winner of the "Winter Championship" has gone on to take the overall league title at the end of the season on 43 occasions.
It took a last-minute goal from Marco Franceschetti, following Roberto Mancini's cheeky backheel to keep Sampdoria within a point of Juventus.
The goal, given despite claims for off-side from Florentine players, cancelled out Gabriele Batistuta's 31st-minute penalty.
The Argentine, who had missed his two previous spotkicks, scored his eighth goal of the season after picking himself up from a foul in the area.
At the San Siro stadium, the ghosts of Inter's recent, inglorious past came back to haunt Roy Hodgson's side.
Three of the players dumped by the club following last season's poor performances -- Davide Fontolan, Andrea Seno and Russia's Igor Shalimov -- played key roles in Bologna's win.
First, Fontolan laid on the cross from which Giancarlo Marocchi fired the visitors in front in the 38th minute.
Then, second-half substitute Shalimov rounded two players and goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca for the last-minute goal that gave Bologna their first victory since November 1996.
"Our championship ambitions remain intact," a resilient Hodgson told reporters after the match.
Roberto Baggio, reportedly at odds with Milan coach Arrigo Sacchi off-the-field, came to his manager's aid on Sunday.
When Baggio was brought on as a second-half substitute, Milan were heading for their first defeat at Cagliari in 25 years thanks to Sandro Tovalieri's 44th-minute goal.
But in the 65th minute, Baggio showed a glimpse of his old magic, dribbling to the by-line before setting-up Frenchman Christophe Dugarry for his second goal in successive matches.
Milan now lie sixth in the league.
Fourth-placed Vicenza raced into a two-goal lead at home to Napoli, Roberto Murgita and Uruguay's Marcelo Otero finding the net inside the opening 30 minutes.
But French defender Alain Boghossian signalled a Napoli revival, resolving a goalmouth scramble in the 37th minute.
After the break, the visitors earned a deserved point through Fabio Pecchia's 55th-minute equaliser.
The draw left Vicenza level on 27 points with Parma, who pulled off their fourth successive win, a 1-0 victory over Verona.

Serie A's top scorer Filippo Inzaghi scored his 11th goal of the season in Atalanta's 1-0 victory over Reggiana, a result that puts Emilio Mondonico's shoestring side ahead of Carlos Bianchi's expensively assembled Roma, beaten 1-0 at Udinese.
